_note: Scripted Chapter 1 plot beats, fired through the event scheduler. armedBy means the beat waits for a flag before it can be scheduled; atTick beats fire regardless of player state, per eventScheduler.js's remit. The finale plays out through this system rather than a bespoke mechanic — same as the Mayor's death and the Chapter 2 invasion.

beats._note: The Mayor takes office. Introduces resources and the dashboard, nothing political yet.
Teaches the priority ladder at the moment it first matters, not in a tutorial before it does.
Law arrives as punctuation, roughly ten minutes in. Before this the player has only run the Shaft.
Meet the four department elders, including the Chair, presented as a facilitator nobody envies. The player will replay this scene in memory after the finale.

The leads converge; the Chair is caught executing something behind the Mayor's back. The catch is real and so is the trap. Before killing the Mayor the Chair confesses, against his own will: the Mayor was never in control, and the Chair is as much a puppet as anyone. delayTicks is the gap between arming and firing — the player has four minutes of ordinary work left and does not know it.

Chapter beats must fire regardless of player state. A player who never investigates still reaches Chapter 2 — the Chair simply acts first, and the confession lands on someone who never suspected a thing. Arguably the better version of the scene.
